brief: Goldman Sachs European equity sales note covering Thursday's close and the desk's open items. US equities fell as higher oil and a continued backup in yields weighed on risk: SPX -58bps to 7591, NDX -108bps, RTY -104bps, VIX +8.4% to 17.84, 10-year Treasury yield the highest since November 2023. Europe closed at its lowest since 8 July, with oil and shipping baskets bid on disruption fears and the GS global copper basket -5.6% after Reuters reported a delayed US tariff decision. Hedge funds and long-only accounts each finished $1bn net sellers. The desk estimates systematic equity positioning at $421bn, close to five-year highs, and short-term CTA thresholds on NDX, SPX and RTY have all broken, adding to the European index break earlier in the week. Gamma at spot is still supportive because the street is long, but the desk models a flip to negative on a roughly 200bps selloff. GS keeps a 25bps December ECB hike, pushes cuts to 2027Q4 and 2028Q1 and lifts its terminal rate forecast to 2.25%. Conference takes: Nvidia Buy with a $300 target, Dell replacement demand and component tightness, Intesa preferred to Caixa, Sell Lindt on European food cost deflation moderating.
